title: No One to Blame: A Framework of Constitutive AI Unaccountability
abstract: arXiv:2608.12104v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The increasing deployment of autonomous, agentic AI systems challenges traditional accountability mechanisms. Existing research predominantly frames AI accountability gaps as barriers that can be overcome through better standards, transparency, and institutional reform. We argue that this framing is insufficient: certain configurations of actors, systems, and institutions render AI accountability conceptually unachievable regardless of effort. We introduce the concept of constitutive AI unaccountability to capture these configurations. Through a three-stage qualitative study comprising a concept-centric literature analysis, a secondary analysis of 27 expert interviews with AI professionals from technical, legal, and sociotechnical backgrounds, and an illustrative framework application to the open-source agentic AI system OpenClaw, we identify nine categories and 20 themes of constitutive AI unaccountability. translated_title: 无人可责：建构性AI不可问责性的框架
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.12104v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：自主、代理型AI系统的日益部署挑战了传统的问责机制。现有研究主要将AI问责差距视为可以通过更好的标准、透明度和制度改革来克服的障碍。我们认为这种框架是不充分的：某些行动者、系统和制度的配置使AI问责在概念上无法实现，无论付出多大努力。我们引入了“建构性AI不可问责性”这一概念来捕捉这些配置。通过一项三阶段的定性研究，包括以概念为中心文献分析、对来自技术、法律和社会技术背景的AI专业人员的27次专家访谈的二次分析，以及一个对开源代理型AI系统OpenClaw的说明性框架应用，我们识别出建构性AI不可问责性的九个类别和二十个主题。这些内容被组织在三个维度中。
tldr: 本文提出“建构性AI不可问责性”概念，指出某些AI系统配置使问责在概念上无法实现，并通过三阶段研究识别出九类二十种相关主题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the concept of "constitutive AI unaccountability," arguing that certain configurations of AI systems make accountability conceptually unachievable, and identifies nine categories and twenty themes through a three-stage study.
